notes: Polybius reports more than 150,000 infantry and 6,000 cavalry deployed in Italy. This is not his much larger register of men liable for service.

scope: Romans and Italian allies under arms
notes: Livy's twenty-five citizen legions are expanded with allied formations; Devereaux independently describes roughly a quarter-million men under arms after 216 BCE.
Modern reconstruction from Tacitus's disposition of twenty-five legions, a broadly comparable auxiliary establishment, and the Rome garrison; fleets are excluded.
Hassall's reconstruction of the Principate army near its high point; this is an establishment estimate rather than a count of soldiers concentrated in one theater.
MacMullen's reconstruction of the late imperial army. It is a paper-strength estimate assembled from fragmentary unit evidence.
Elton's lower reconstruction for the Constantinian army; published totals differ sharply because unit strengths and included categories are uncertain.

Treadgold converts the eastern Notitia's listed units to 303,000 soldiers. He dates the structure to c. 395; Kaldellis and Kruse argue that the five-army system emerged only in the 440s, a redating that remains debated. Plotted at 440 to avoid presenting the traditional date as settled.
